question: Should the registry-backed node-hosted plugin-tool contract in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90431 fully satisfy this issue, or must paired nodes also be allowed to advertise standalone raw tool schemas?
rationale: The proven PR uses Gateway-installed plugin metadata as the authority for model-visible tool definitions, while the issue requests node-owned definitions without a plugin; source evidence cannot choose that product and security boundary.

options.title: Accept registry-backed contract
options.body: Land the linked PR and close this issue afterward, with Gateway-known plugin descriptors as the only supported dynamic node-tool authority.

options.title: Add standalone schemas
options.body: Keep a separate design open for raw node definitions with explicit provenance, naming, collision, authorization, schema validation, and tool-policy semantics.

options.title: Keep existing architecture
options.body: Reject dynamic node tools and continue using wrapper plugins plus the generic `nodes` tool.

recommendation.title: Accept registry-backed contract
recommendation.body: Land the linked PR and close this issue afterward, with Gateway-known plugin descriptors as the only supported dynamic node-tool authority.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the active implementation, its proof, and the recent central-file history for this trust boundary.
